clue.text: Centre of attraction in ancient city

definitions.meaning: any place that draws crowds of devotees or visitors
the holy city in Arabia, birthplace of Muhammad

explanation.definitionFit: The holy city's role as a pilgrimage goal gave its name to any place drawing many visitors.

clue.text: Travelling oysterman found order here?

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters of oysterman are on the move into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A roving seller of oysters stumbles on a religious community.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious order of monks lives in such a community building, so that is where you would find one.

clue.text: Actors in speaking class

indicators.note: in speaking signals that a word is said out loud and a different spelling is meant

parts.note: the actors of a play together form its cast

explanation.surface: Performers take part in an elocution lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary social class, especially in Hindu society, is a caste.

clue.text: Adventurous girl embraces worker in Spanish resort

indicators.note: embraces means the girl's name wraps around the other piece

parts.note: Alice has adventures in Wonderland
a worker ant is the stock crossword worker

explanation.surface: A daring young woman hugs a labourer at a holiday town in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A port city on Spain's Costa Blanca, popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: Certain secretarial work curtailed as security measure

parts.note: safe, as in a safe bet, means certain

indicators.note: curtailed means the word loses its tail, its final letter

parts.note: typing is the work of a secretary

explanation.surface: A clerical job cut short is taken as a safeguard.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin with a guarded point fastens clothing securely, a small safety device.

clue.text: 50% in prison are informers

indicators.note: 50% means just half of the prison's name is used

parts.note: ... ... is a famous prison in New York State

explanation.surface: Half the inmates of a jail are grasses.
explanation.definitionFit: To sing is slang for informing to the police, so those who sing are informers.

clue.text: Source of cheap jumpers?

parts.note: reads as a bargain place for knitted sweaters, but the jumpers are leaping insects

explanation.surface: Where can you buy bargain sweaters?
explanation.definitionFit: A street market of cheap second-hand goods, punningly a market for leaping parasites.

clue.text: Apocryphal character raised infants at first in shoe

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the turned shoe
raised in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sabot is a wooden shoe

indicators.note: at first selects the first letter of infants

explanation.surface: A figure from the Apocrypha lifted children into a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobias, son of Tobit, is a hero of the Book of Tobit in the Apocrypha.

clue.text: Measuring device man's put outside observatory roof

indicators.note: put outside means the man's name goes around the roof

parts.note: Peter is a man's name
an observatory is typically topped by a dome

explanation.surface: A man installs a gauge on top of a stargazing building.
explanation.definitionFit: This device counts a walker's steps to measure distance travelled.

clue.text: Called up soldier to kill heartlessly

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to man a post is to soldier it; a man is a private soldier

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: to end a life is to kill

explanation.surface: A soldier is summoned to kill without mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: Named and called both mean given a name or designated.

clue.text: Having no knowledge of destroyed cine scene

definitions.note: noun sense: the state of having no knowledge, ignorance

indicators.note: destroyed suggests the words cine and scene are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone is unaware that a film sequence was wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary word for ignorance, the lack of knowledge.

clue.text: Obscure plot I am following

parts.note: a flower bed is a garden plot
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: A scheme comes after me.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure is to dim or darken, which is the archaic sense of this verb.

clue.text: Go up and down to visit Maxim

parts.note: to see someone is to visit them
a saw is an old saying or maxim

explanation.surface: Bob about when calling on a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground plank that rocks so each end rises and falls; as a verb, to oscillate.

clue.text: Ancient Egyptian state

parts.note: looks like a kingdom of the pharaohs, but describes the preserved condition of a mummy

explanation.surface: A kingdom of the pharaohs.
explanation.definitionFit: Egyptian mummies were preserved with spices and resins, the state of a preserved corpse.

clue.text: Frozen assets? Children will think so!

definitions.text: Frozen assets? Children will think so!

parts.words: Frozen assets? Children will think so!
parts.note: frozen assets sounds like blocked funds, but lolly is slang for money and children treasure frozen treats

explanation.surface: Blocked funds, and kids would agree.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen flavoured treats on sticks, which children value highly; lolly is also British slang for money.

clue.text: Set and cast are repositioned in shooting breaks

indicators.note: repositioned tells us the letters of the three words are moved into new places

explanation.surface: Film sets and actors are moved during breaks in shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: A shooting brake (also spelt break) is an old British name for an estate car, originally a vehicle for a hunting party.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting brake is the old British term for a station wagon.

clue.text: Figure offered by corporation accepting a prize novel

indicators.note: accepting means the belly word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: corporation is jocular slang for a paunch, a tum

indicators.note: novel signals the letters of a and prize are arranged in a new way

explanation.surface: A company hands out an award for fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company but is old jocular slang for a pot belly; 'offered by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometrical figure: a quadrilateral, with one pair of parallel sides in British usage.

clue.text: Young men went West — to here

definitions.text: Young men went West — to here

parts.words: Young men went West — to here
parts.note: echoes the advice go west, young man; the Mormon pioneers trekked west to settle this territory

explanation.surface: Youths heading west ended up here.
explanation.definitionFit: The western US state settled by Mormon pioneers who journeyed west.

clue.text: American author in Mayflower, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard rather than seen, spelt differently

parts.note: the hawthorn is called mayflower because it blooms in May

explanation.surface: A US writer aboard the Pilgrim Fathers' ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mayflower is not the ship but the may tree's blossom.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel Hawthorne wrote The Scarlet Letter.

clue.text: A bustlin', chaotic city

indicators.note: chaotic says the letters of the two words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A busy, disordered metropolis.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkey's largest city, on the Bosphorus.

clue.text: Rhino in a China shop

parts.note: plays on bull in a china shop; rhino is old slang for money, and this is what money is called in a Chinese shop

explanation.surface: A large beast wrecking a crockery store.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency unit of China, so the cash spent in a shop there.

clue.text: Method of securing bridge partnership in all-English team

indicators.note: in places the partnership inside the rest of the pieces

parts.note: all plus E, the abbreviation for English
a crew is a team, as of rowers
North and South are a partnership at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A tactic to win a bridge pairing in a side made up only of English players.
explanation.definitionFit: A fastening with a hexagonal socket in its head, turned by a key.

clue.text: What could be thrown out by Charon?

definitions.text: What could be thrown out by Charon?

indicators.note: thrown out means the letters of the boatman's name are scattered and reset

explanation.surface: What might the ferryman of the dead throw overboard?
explanation.walkthrough: Charon is the ferryman of the Underworld in Greek myth; a boatman might throw this out to moor.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy weight thrown from a boat to hold it in place.

clue.text: Sucker is both naive and knowing

parts.note: green means inexperienced or naive
fly is British slang for knowing or sharp

explanation.surface: A dupe is at once innocent and shrewd.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphid, an insect that sucks plant sap.

clue.text: Information influencing children initially is this

definitions.text: Information influencing children initially is this

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: initially selects the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Inherited data that shapes young people.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to genes, the hereditary information that shapes offspring.

clue.text: Gumshoe's expression of surprise as Capone breaks in

indicators.note: breaks in means one piece bursts into the other

parts.note: gosh is an exclamation of surprise
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A detective gasps as the gangster bursts in.
explanation.walkthrough: Gumshoe looks like a private eye, but it is literally a rubber shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber overshoe, worn over ordinary footwear in wet weather.

clue.text: Eye dispenser of-short measure

definitions.meaning: relating to the eye or sight; also a lens of an instrument
a device on an upturned bottle in a bar that releases a fixed tot of spirits

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective concerns vision; in British pubs the bar device measuring spirits has the same name.

clue.text: A year without church is causing ill-feeling

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the other pieces go around church

explanation.surface: Missing church for a year is creating resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside'; ill-feeling is read as feeling ill, not resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Aching all over, a sore, unwell sensation.

clue.text: Arab's cry in near East

indicators.note: in tells us one letter goes inside the word for near

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

explanation.surface: A call from someone in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: The Arab is a breed of horse, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry of a horse, such as an Arab steed.

clue.text: Raising equipment inside island peak

parts.note: in means inside
Cuba is a Caribbean island
a tor is a rocky hilltop

explanation.surface: Lifting gear on a mountain on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus for rearing premature babies or hatching eggs, raising in the sense of bringing up.

clue.text: Avoiding publicity, arrived hastily, left concealed

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: concealed means the letter for left is hidden away, so dropped

parts.note: rashly means hastily

explanation.surface: A celebrity dodging the press turned up in a hurry and slipped away unseen.
explanation.definitionFit: Reluctant to be photographed or to appear in the public eye.

clue.text: What can be said to shut up a philosopher?

indicators.note: can be said signals the word is heard aloud, a different spelling meant

parts.note: to lock is to shut up securely

explanation.surface: What words can silence a thinker?
explanation.definitionFit: John Locke was the English Enlightenment philosopher.
